A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original verification and test-time-scaling experiments. Appendix C includes additional difficulty-stratified results and reasoning-model evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original error analyses, robustness evaluations, model-selection experiments, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The core generative-verification and response-filtering procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D adds auxiliary procedures for entropy-based difficulty estimation and generator/verifier selection using validation-set balanced accuracy, making earlier deployment suggestions more operational.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 benchmarks covering mathematical reasoning, knowledge, and natural-language reasoning, with 2,347, 1,196, and 901 problems respectively. The added analyses change procedures and model configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: The original model comparisons and reasoning-model variants are retained. v2 adds Qwen3-235B verification results and evaluates solve-then-verify and step-by-step prompt alternatives (D.3–D.4). Its new TTS selection experiments also use Qwen3-32B as a fixed verifier alongside GPT-4o.

E3.justification: The original 64-response pools and eight-response verification subsampling remain. New experiments introduce 50/50 validation/test splits for model selection, majority-vote accuracy, FLOPs and token-cost evaluation, and difficulty stratification estimated from eight Qwen2.5-3B responses (D.1–D.2, D.5). These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative analyses of verifier solving mistakes and generator surface-level errors (Figures 3 and 5), robustness checks using estimated difficulty, larger models and alternative prompts, and model-selection/cost analyses (Appendix D). The earlier reasoning-model analyses and illustrative cases are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces 10,000 bootstrap resamples and 95% confidence intervals for the two added error analyses. This uncertainty reporting is confined to those analyses; the original RQ2 procedure of averaging eight random-subsampling repetitions remains unchanged.

E6.justification: New results quantify solving mistakes, surface-level errors, robustness, and held-out model-selection outcomes. Table 2 adds token measurements, including 193 GPT-4o tokens per prompt for verification versus 482 for generation. Existing principal heatmap values are retained, while the abstract's reported Gemma performance-gap closure changes from 75.5% to 75.7%.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds the mathematical definition of normalized answer-entropy difficulty, H/log K, including its bounds and endpoint interpretation. Existing pass-rate, difficulty, verification, and TTS definitions are otherwise retained or expressed more compactly; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three verification findings and the same TTS conclusions about generator convergence and limited advantages from stronger verifiers. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 strengthens the case-based explanation of false negatives through solving-mistake attribution and expands explanations of difficulty-dependent capability regimes (C.4). It adds cost-aware selection guidance and drops v1's categorical assertion that the bottleneck is not model capacity, while retaining the principal verification limitations.

D1.justification: v2 supplies additional verification and error-analysis prompt templates, judge identities, sampling details, and computational-cost assumptions. It also specifies the Qwen3-235B checkpoint and decoding settings and newly documents reasoning-model sampling parameters. The original RQ2 sampling description is relocated to B.4, rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions the study alongside concurrent work by Lu et al. on cross-family verification, adds sources supporting difficulty estimation and error analysis, and removes the earlier self-preference-bias discussion and associated citations. The central positioning relative to capability–verification research remains intact; publication-year updates alone are not substantive changes.

P1.justification: Related work and preliminaries are substantially condensed, results and TTS discussions are rewritten, and detailed RQ2 procedures move to the appendix. The appendices are reorganized into expanded setup, separate generator/verifier analyses, extended studies, and relocated case studies, with a contents list and new statements.

P2.justification: v2 adds mechanism-analysis plots, robustness and efficiency figures, and two tables. Main-text TTS figures are reorganized into mathematics-focused displays, with the earlier multi-domain material retained in the appendix. Several existing figures are resized, relocated, or reduced to selected panels, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens two weaknesses in v1: mechanisms supported mainly by illustrative cases, and efficiency implications inferred from accuracy alone. Quantitative error analyses with confidence intervals, difficulty/prompt/model robustness checks, and held-out selection and cost experiments provide substantial additional support. Cost conclusions remain qualified by the assumed GPT-4o parameter count and model-specific token accounting, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger evidence and practical validation.
